paras.en: That was when the fox appeared.
paras.zh: 就在这时，狐狸出现了。

paras.en: “Hello,” said the fox.
paras.zh: “你好。”狐狸说。

paras.en: “Hello,” replied the little prince politely. He turned round but saw nothing.
paras.zh: “你好。”小王子礼貌地回答，转过身去，却什么也没看见。

paras.en: “I’m here,” said the voice, “under the apple tree.”
paras.zh: “我在这里，”那个声音说，“在苹果树下。”

paras.en: “Who are you?” said the little prince. “You’re very pretty…”
paras.zh: “你是谁？”小王子说，“你真好看……”

paras.en: “I’m a fox,” said the fox.
paras.zh: “我是一只狐狸。”狐狸说。

paras.en: “Come and play with me,” the little prince suggested. “I’m so sad…”
paras.zh: “来和我一起玩吧，”小王子向他提议，“我好难过……”

paras.en: “I can’t play with you,” said the fox. “I haven’t been tamed.”
paras.zh: “我不能和你一起玩，”狐狸说，“我还没有被驯服。”

paras.en: “Oh! I’m sorry,” said the little prince.
paras.zh: “啊！对不起。”小王子说。

paras.en: But after thinking it over, he added:
paras.zh: 可是想了想，他又补充道：

paras.en: “What does ‘tame’ mean?”
paras.zh: “‘驯服’是什么意思？”

paras.en: “You’re not from here,” said the fox. “What are you looking for?”
paras.zh: “你不是这里的人，”狐狸说，“你在找什么？”

paras.en: “I’m looking for people,” said the little prince. “What does ‘tame’ mean?”
paras.zh: “我在找人，”小王子说，“‘驯服’是什么意思？”

paras.en: “People,” said the fox, “have guns and they hunt. That’s such a nuisance! They also keep hens. That’s the only interesting thing about them. Are you looking for hens?”
paras.zh: “人啊，”狐狸说，“他们有枪，还会打猎。真叫人头疼！他们也养母鸡。他们只有这一点有意思。你在找母鸡吗？”

paras.en: “No,” said the little prince. “I’m looking for friends. What does ‘tame’ mean?”
paras.zh: “不是，”小王子说，“我在找朋友。‘驯服’是什么意思？”

paras.en: “It’s something too often forgotten,” said the fox. “It means ‘To form bonds...’”
paras.zh: “这是一件太常被遗忘的事，”狐狸说，“意思是‘建立牵绊……’”

paras.en: “Form bonds?”
paras.zh: “建立牵绊？”

paras.en: “Of course,” said the fox. “To me, you’re still only a little boy just like a hundred thousand little boys. And I don’t need you. And you don’t need me either. To you, I’m only a fox like a hundred thousand foxes. But if you tame me, we will need each other. To me, you will be unique in the world. To you, I will be unique in the world...”
paras.zh: “当然，”狐狸说，“对我来说，你还只是个小男孩，跟十万个小男孩完全一样。而我不需要你。而你也不需要我。对你来说，我只是一只狐狸，跟十万只狐狸一样。可是，如果你驯服了我，我们就会彼此需要。对我来说，你将是世上独一无二的。对你来说，我将是世上独一无二的……”

paras.en: “I’m beginning to understand,” said the little prince. “There’s a flower... I think she’s tamed me...”
paras.zh: “我开始明白了，”小王子说，“有一朵花……我想她已经驯服了我……”

paras.en: “That’s possible,” said the fox. “You see all sorts of things on Earth...”
paras.zh: “有这个可能，”狐狸说，“地球上什么样的事都见得到……”

paras.en: “Oh! It's not on Earth,” said the little prince. The fox looked very intrigued:
paras.zh: “哦！那不是在地球上。”小王子说。狐狸显得十分好奇：

paras.en: “On another planet?”
paras.zh: “在另一颗星球上？”

paras.en: “Yes.”
paras.zh: “是的。”

paras.en: “Are there hunters on that planet?”
paras.zh: “那颗星球上有猎人吗？”

paras.en: “No.”
paras.zh: “没有。”

paras.en: “Now that's interesting! And hens?”
paras.zh: “这倒有意思！那有母鸡吗？”

paras.en: “No.”
paras.zh: “没有。”

paras.en: “Nothing is perfect,” sighed the fox.
paras.zh: “没有什么是十全十美的。”狐狸叹了口气。

paras.en: But the fox came back to his idea:
paras.zh: 不过，狐狸又说回了自己的想法：

paras.en: “My life is monotonous. I hunt hens, and men hunt me. All hens look alike, and all men look alike. So I get a little bored. But if you tame me, it will be as though sunshine has filled my life. I will know a sound of footsteps different from all the others. Other footsteps send me back underground. Yours will call me out of my burrow, like music. And then look! Do you see the wheat fields over there? I don't eat bread. Wheat is no use to me. Wheat fields remind me of nothing. And that's sad! But your hair is the colour of gold. So it will be wonderful when you have tamed me! The wheat, which is golden, will remind me of you. And I will love the sound of the wind in the wheat...”
paras.zh: “我的生活很单调。我捕猎母鸡，人捕猎我。所有的母鸡都长得一样，所有的人也都长得一样。所以我有点无聊。可是，如果你驯服我，我的生活就会像有了阳光一样。我会认得一种脚步声，和所有别的脚步声都不同。别的脚步声会让我躲回地下。你的脚步声却会像音乐一样，唤我走出洞穴。还有，你看！你看见那边的麦田了吗？我不吃面包。麦子对我没有用。麦田也不会让我想起什么。这多让人难过啊！可是，你的头发是金子般的颜色。那么，等你驯服了我，一切就会多么美好！金色的麦子会让我想起你。我也会喜欢上风吹过麦田的声音……”

paras.en: The fox fell silent and looked at the little prince for a long time:
paras.zh: 狐狸不说话了，久久地望着小王子：

paras.en: “Please... tame me!” he said.
paras.zh: “求求你……驯服我吧！”他说。

paras.en: “I'd like to,” replied the little prince, “but I don't have much time. I have friends to discover and many things to get to know.”
paras.zh: “我愿意，”小王子回答，“可是我的时间不多。我还有朋友要去结识，还有许多事物要去了解。”

paras.en: “You only know the things you tame,” said the fox. “People no longer have time to get to know anything. They buy ready-made things from merchants. But since there are no merchants selling friends, people no longer have friends. If you want a friend, tame me!”
paras.zh: “只有驯服了的事物，才是你了解的事物，”狐狸说，“人们已经没有时间去了解任何东西了。他们从商贩那里买现成的东西。可是，没有卖朋友的商贩，所以人们也就不再有朋友了。要是你想要一个朋友，就驯服我吧！”

paras.en: “What must I do?” said the little prince.
paras.zh: “我该怎么做呢？”小王子说。

paras.en: “You must be very patient,” replied the fox. “First you'll sit a little distance from me, like that, in the grass. I'll watch you out of the corner of my eye, and you won't say anything. Language is a source of misunderstandings. But each day you'll be able to sit a little closer...”
paras.zh: “你得很有耐心，”狐狸回答，“起先，你要坐得离我远一点，就像这样，坐在草丛里。我会用眼角看着你，你什么也不要说。语言是误解的源头。不过，每一天，你都可以坐得更近一点……”

paras.en: The next day the little prince came back.
paras.zh: 第二天，小王子又来了。

paras.en: “It would have been better to come back at the same time,” said the fox. “If you come at four in the afternoon, for example, I'll begin to feel happy as early as three. The nearer the hour comes, the happier I'll feel. By four I'll already be restless and worried; I'll discover the price of happiness! But if you come at any time at all, I'll never know when to dress my heart... We need rituals.”
paras.zh: “你要是在同一个时间回来就更好了，”狐狸说，“比如说，你下午四点来，那从三点起，我就会开始快乐。时间越近，我就会越快乐。到了四点，我已经会坐立不安，担心起来；我会明白幸福的代价！可是，如果你什么时候来都不一定，我就永远不知道，该在什么时候给我的心穿戴整齐……得有仪式才行。”

paras.en: “What is a ritual?” said the little prince.
paras.zh: “什么是仪式？”小王子说。

paras.en: “That's another thing too often forgotten,” said the fox. “It's what makes one day different from other days, one hour from other hours. My hunters have a ritual, for example. On Thursdays they dance with the village girls. So Thursday is a wonderful day! I go for a walk as far as the vineyard. If the hunters danced at any time at all, the days would all be alike, and I'd have no holidays.”
paras.zh: “这也是一件太容易被人遗忘的事，”狐狸说，“它让某一天不同于别的日子，让某一个小时不同于别的小时。比如，那些追猎我的猎人就有一种仪式。每逢星期四，他们和村里的姑娘们跳舞。于是，星期四就成了美妙的一天！我出去散步，一直走到葡萄园。如果猎人们随时都跳舞，那么每一天就都一样了，我也就没有假期了。”

paras.en: So the little prince tamed the fox. And when the time to leave drew near:
paras.zh: 就这样，小王子驯服了狐狸。而当离别的时刻临近时：

paras.en: “Ah!” said the fox. “...I’ll cry.”
paras.zh: “啊！”狐狸说，“……我会哭的。”

paras.en: “It’s your fault,” said the little prince. “I didn’t wish you any harm, but you wanted me to tame you...”
paras.zh: “这得怪你自己，”小王子说，“我一点也不想伤害你，可是你要我驯服你……”

paras.en: “Of course,” said the fox.
paras.zh: “当然，”狐狸说。

paras.en: “But you’re going to cry!” said the little prince.
paras.zh: “可你会哭的！”小王子说。

paras.en: “Of course,” said the fox.
paras.zh: “当然，”狐狸说。

paras.en: “Then you gain nothing from it!”
paras.zh: “那你什么也没得到呀！”

paras.en: “I do gain something,” said the fox, “because of the colour of the wheat.”
paras.zh: “我得到了，”狐狸说，“因为麦子的颜色。”

paras.en: Then he added:
paras.zh: 接着，他又说：

paras.en: “Go and see the roses again. You’ll understand that yours is unique in all the world. You’ll come back to say goodbye to me, and I’ll give you a secret as a gift.”
paras.zh: “再去看看那些玫瑰吧。你会明白，你的那一朵在世上是独一无二的。你会回来向我告别，那时我会送你一个秘密当礼物。”

paras.en: The little prince went off to see the roses again.
paras.zh: 小王子又去看那些玫瑰了。

paras.en: “You are not at all like my rose. You are nothing yet,” he told them. “No one has tamed you, and you have tamed no one. You are as my fox once was. He was just a fox like a hundred thousand others. But I made him my friend, and now he is unique in the world.”
paras.zh: “你们和我的玫瑰一点也不像，你们还什么都不是，”他对她们说。“没有谁驯服过你们，你们也没有驯服过谁。你们就像我的狐狸从前那样。他原本只是一只狐狸，和其他十万只狐狸没有两样。可是我让他成了我的朋友，如今他在世界上就独一无二了。”

paras.en: And the roses felt embarrassed.
paras.zh: 那些玫瑰都不好意思了。

paras.en: “You are beautiful, but you are empty,” he told them again. “No one could die for you. Of course, an ordinary passer-by would think my own rose looked like you. But she alone is more important than all of you, because she is the one I watered. Because she is the one I put under a glass globe. Because she is the one I sheltered behind the screen. Because she is the one whose caterpillars I killed (except for the two or three I spared so there could be butterflies). Because she is the one I listened to as she complained, or boasted, or even sometimes fell silent. Because she is my rose.”
paras.zh: “你们很美，可是你们是空的，”他又对她们说。“人不能为你们而死。当然，一个普通的过路人会觉得，我的那朵玫瑰和你们很像。可她单单一朵，就比你们所有的玫瑰都重要，因为我浇过水的是她。因为我放在玻璃罩下的是她。因为我用屏风挡护的是她。因为我杀死的毛毛虫是她身上的（只留下两三条，为了能有蝴蝶）。因为我听她抱怨，或是夸口，甚至有时听她沉默，而那都是她。因为她是我的玫瑰。”

paras.en: And he came back to the fox:
paras.zh: 于是他回到狐狸身边：

paras.en: “Goodbye,” he said…
paras.zh: “再见了，”他说……

paras.en: “Goodbye,” said the fox. “Here is my secret. It is very simple: One sees clearly only with the heart. What is essential is invisible to the eyes.”
paras.zh: “再见了，”狐狸说。“这就是我的秘密。它很简单：只有用心，才能看得清。真正重要的东西，用眼睛是看不见的。”

paras.en: “What matters most cannot be seen by the eyes,” the little prince repeated, so that he would remember.
paras.zh: “最重要的东西，眼睛看不见，”小王子重复了一遍，好让自己记住。

paras.en: “The time you have wasted on your rose is what makes your rose so important.”
paras.zh: “正是你为你的玫瑰耗费的时间，才让你的玫瑰变得如此重要。”

paras.en: “The time I have wasted on my rose…” said the little prince, so that he would remember.
paras.zh: “是我为我的玫瑰浪费的时间……”小王子说，好让自己记住。

paras.en: “People have forgotten this truth,” said the fox. “But you must not forget it. Once you have tamed something, you become responsible for it for ever. You are responsible for your rose…”
paras.zh: “人们已经忘了这个道理，”狐狸说，“但你不能忘。一旦你驯服了什么，你就要永远对它负责。你要对你的玫瑰负责……”

paras.en: “I am responsible for my rose…” repeated the little prince, so that he would remember.
paras.zh: “我要对我的玫瑰负责……”小王子重复了一遍，好让自己记住。
